sources_considered.why: Controlled contamination research distinguishes memorization from using memorized data to improve scores.
Contemporaneous developer audit supplies material evidence against assuming that detected contamination substantially inflated exam scores.
Search identified a later contamination experiment, but it does not supply the required matched 2019–August 2023 comparison.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Inbal Magar and Roy Schwartz
evidence_items.explanation: Controlled experiments found that contamination could improve downstream results, but memorization did not always produce that improvement. This establishes a possible mechanism without measuring a deterioration from 2019 to 2023.

OpenAI reported little change after removing detected contaminated exam questions. Its audit acknowledged detection limitations and did not provide the longitudinal comparison needed to contradict the full claim.

unresolved_gaps: No matched 2019–2023 study was found that isolates expanded training exposure as the cause of declining benchmark predictive validity.
The evidence does not quantify the relationship between benchmark scores and intelligence generally.
